Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden surge of 429s this morning

Quick triage notes (ops):
- Root cause (prelim): a deploy of the capacity-flag-rotation job at ~08:30 UTC flipped the per-project tier flag for several HealthByte projects. A bug in the alias mapping caused those projects to inherit a low-rate plan (dev-tier) rather than the customer's reserved pool.
- Symptom: sudden drop in token throughput allowance per project -> immediate 429s. HealthByte SDKs retried without jitter which amplified load (retry storm).
- Confirmed mapping mismatch in quota service: org_alias -> project_id mapping returned null for projects with specific labels. I attached the mapping export (quota_mapping.csv).

Immediate mitigation planned: revert the flag-rotation at quota-service at 10:15 UTC (rollback already staged), and enable an emergency override to route healthbyte-main projects to dedicated pool while we validate. Also recommend applying a temporary global retry-throttle gate for affected org so SDKs receive Retry-After guidance instead of blind retries.

I'll start rollback now and post a timeline.

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- 11:15 UTC: global retry-throttle gate enabled for org=healthbyte-main (clients now receive Retry-After headers).
